featured_reviews.name: Fatema P
featured_reviews.review_text:
A delightful meal at Flavors of Malvan in Prabhadevi! The food is exceptionally tasty, wholesome, and prepared in a way that feels truly home-style, yet packed with authentic coastal flavors.

The Green Chutney Surmai was outstanding, the Fish Curry with rice was comforting and flavorful, and the Koliwada Prawns were perfectly cooked and absolutely delicious. To top it all, the Kokum Soda was simply mind-blowing—refreshing, tangy, and the perfect accompaniment to the meal.

A special mention to Vinod and Navin, who were incredibly warm, welcoming, and attentive. They took the time to understand our preferences and suggested dishes that suited our tastes perfectly, making the dining experience even more enjoyable.

If you're looking for authentic Malvani cuisine that combines traditional flavors with heartfelt hospitality, this place is a must-visit!The restaurant is Flavors of Malvan.

featured_reviews.name: Sankar Kasirajan
featured_reviews.review_text:
It was my daughter's birthday eve, and after some gentle persuasion to choose Pallavi's boutique café over Mumbai stalwarts like Trishna or Mahesh, we were seated in this beautifully done-up spot near Dadar's Shivaji Park. Though small, the space possesses a premium, fine-dining ambiance.

The Feast
Despite claiming to be "light eaters" (ahem!), we indulged in a vast selection, and every single dish was amazing. The true "Flavours" of Malwan shone through, outperforming many other seafood restaurants I've visited over the past 28 years (including Gajalee, Mahesh Lunch Home, and Sindhudurg).
Our order included:
	Refreshing Drinks: Sol Kadi, Kokum Soda, and Lemon Soda.
	Signature Seafood: Chutney Stuffed Pomfret Fry with Prawns, Chutney Stuffed Bombil Roll with Prawns, Sukka Crab, Tisrya Sukka, and Prawn Curry, paired with Rice Bhakri.
	Desserts: Ukdiche Modak and Puran Poli.

The Unforgettable Star
While every item was a feast for the taste buds, the Sukka Crab was the undisputed champion—absolutely outstanding! We literally wiped the plates clean and even drank the leftover Prawn Curry. This is food made with passion; food that truly leaves a lasting memory.

My words and photos simply cannot do full justice to the culinary magic at "Flavours of Malwan."

Don't just read about it—experience the authentic, soulful taste of Malwani cuisine for yourself!

featured_reviews.name: Anvi Kaale
featured_reviews.review_text: I recently had lunch at this restaurant and it was truly a fantastic experience! Authentic malvani taste.😋 The flavors were absolutely amazing, and every dish was prepared to perfection. 💯 I highly recommend trying their delicious offerings. Will definitely be back for more! ✨👍

featured_reviews.name: Preeti Parab
featured_reviews.review_text:
The ambience of the restaurant was lovely and cozy. We tried the Bombil Tawa Fry, but it was quite oily. We also ordered the Surmai Thali and Pomfret Thali. Everything in the thali was good except for the fish curry, which unfortunately lacked flavor. Solkadi was fresh and awesome in taste.

For desserts, we tried Modak and Puranpoli. The Modak tasted good, although the outer covering was a bit thick.The Puranpoli, however, was absolutely awesome and definitely a highlight.

Overall, it’s a nice and cozy restaurant, especially for non-vegetarian lovers. 🐟🍽️

featured_reviews.name: Nitin Guddeti
featured_reviews.review_text: Had a wonderful experience at Flavours of Malvan! The Prawns pulav and Bombil Thali were absolutely delicious, packed with authentic Malvani flavors. Fresh seafood, flavorful curries, crispy fry, and refreshing solkadhi made the meal truly satisfying. Highly recommended for seafood lovers looking for an authentic taste of the coast. 🐟🦐😋

featured_reviews.name: Greeshma Gowda
featured_reviews.review_text: Walked into this restaurant when we were in Dadar on a Sunday evening. Its a small restaurant on the ground floor of a residential buidling. There was a waiting time of 30 mins to get in. We ordered the pomfret thalli and crab thalli. The service is slow but it was worth the wait. The crab was soft and well cooked and the gravy was delicious. We also had sweet lime soda and lemon ginger drink. Last we had ukdiche modak which was also tasty.

featured_reviews.name: Meghna Sharma
featured_reviews.review_text:
Everything tasted like it was cooked in someone’s very talented Malvani aaji’s kitchen. The bombil fry? Illegal levels of good. The mutton sukka + the prawn thali? Had me contemplating licking the plate. The puran poli and the modaks? Felt like a hug in dessert form. Just solid recommendations from the team and great vibes all around.
If you like your food flavourful, fiery, and with zero nonsense, this place is a no-brainer. Will 100% be back.

featured_reviews.name: Jimeet Pawaskar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Found my new favorite Sunday spot! Being a Malvani…this place is lovely, understated home-style charm that makes you want to settle in and stay a while.
Even with a 45-minute wait on a Sunday, the staff remained gracious and efficient. The Mutton Special Thali is a must-try—rich, authentic, and perfectly executed. It felt less like eating at a restaurant and more like a high-end home-cooked feast!
Full marks overall !

featured_reviews.name: sonia mehta
featured_reviews.review_text:
It’s been a while since we’ve enjoyed an authentic Maharashtrian meal! At first glance the place makes your feel right at home, very true to its name! We had such a great meal on Sunday, we were three of us - my brother, my sister and I.
The best thing to do when you visit is let the owner suggest their specials for you to eat, we didn’t even open the menu - we tried the Chonak Fry - 10/10, we tried the Bombil fry- 12/10 ( the filling inside the Bombil blew our mind, we had the Alu Wadi with Prawns filling - 10/10!
For main course we had the Amti with Rice Bhakri and Ravas Fry ( the Ravas so incredibly fresh) the main course was 10/10 and to top it off we also tried their Prawns Bhaat / Pulav - it was so damn good! 100/10….the Sol Kadis we tasted took us back home honestly. After this meal all we needed was our bed to sleep on cause we were in a complete food coma. An absolutely outstanding meal with a very comfortable seating and ambiance! A definite must visit again and again!

featured_reviews.name: Naresh Shirodkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Fish Curry Rice is a true celebration of coastal flavours and seafood mastery. Their seafood spread is outstanding — the surmai and pomfret are impeccably fresh, the halwa and bombil melt beautifully, and the fish fry along with the prawns curry are rich, fragrant, and deeply satisfying.

What truly stole the show were the tisrya sukka, mori masala, and kalva sukka — bold, soulful preparations that burst with authentic coastal character. The must-try list is long for a reason: prawns aluwadi, stuffed pomfret, bombil thecha fry, and chounak fry are each crafted with precision and irresistible flavour.

Their thalis deserve special praise — generous, well-balanced, and layered with flavour, offering a complete journey through coastal cuisine. A special mention to owner Sandesh Bhat — the heart and soul of FCR — who ensures taste and consistency are always bang on, and who, along with his attentive team, is always on his toes with spot-on recommendations tailored to your mood and palate.

A place where freshness meets finesse, and every plate tells a story of spice, sea, and tradition.

featured_reviews.review_text: This resturant in primiraly from Pune which is only one in Mumbai Dadar kohinoor is was way beyond expectations .. good try for fish lovers, with great service from staff to decently priced thalis. featured_reviews.name: guptepooja
featured_reviews.review_text:
Excellent place and way better than the Pune branch. It's open from 11.30am to 11pm...so you get served even at 5pm

They cook fresh stuff so order may take time but it's fresh! Amazing taste and super fresh fish. Blessed to have this joint in Dadar which works as a perfect combination of fresh seafood+ authentic goan cuisine+ economical.  We ordered mutton + pomfret fry thali and chicken thali. featured_reviews.name: Sunit Katkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Saw a lot of food vloggers show this place. Big mistake of believing them. Only good thing is the welcome drink called Tival. The prawns sukka was more curry and rubber like prawns. Only slightly better dish was crab masala. Sol kadhi had no kick. Maybe Gajalee and Sindhudurg have spoilt me by giving very good Sol Kadhi. We asked for Rice Bhakri expecting it to be soft like other places. This felt like it was cooked a day before and just reheated and served. It was too hard to be called a rice Bhakri.

Regret not going to Dutta Boarding House in Parel or even Gomantak next door. Had crab masala last week at Dutta Boarding.. FCR does not have that zing but it's better than the rubber prawn sukka taste.

Sorry, will not believe food vloggers from now on.

The food was really good and the ambience was pleasant, making it a nice place to relax and enjoy a meal. Service was also good and the staff were courteous.
One thing to note — the restaurant mentions parking availability, but parking can be difficult since the place is quite inside from the main road.

featured_reviews.name: chinu's kitchen
featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited The Big Fish & Co. on 4th January while I was shopping around Dadar with my mom and sister. While shopping nearby, we asked a local person for a good restaurant recommendation, and she suggested this place — and honestly, it turned out to be a great choice.
Right from the entrance, the experience was pleasant. The security guard at the door was very polite and kind. He asked if we had a reservation (we didn’t), but luckily a few tables were available. Since we were just three people, we were seated comfortably without any wait.
The ambience is quite good — warm, comfortable, and very suitable for families and friends. There were absolutely no negative points when it came to the atmosphere. What really touched my heart was the attentiveness of the staff. They listened carefully, were patient, and ensured everything was smooth. The service was quick, with no unnecessary delays, which I truly appreciated.
Coming to the food — it felt very local and authentic, something I personally connect with. The dishes were unique and well-prepared. We ordered tandoori prawns, which were medium-sized and nicely cooked. I also ordered a thali and a crab dish, both of which were absolutely delicious and the dessert tooo it’s new for me being a konkani
Overall, it was worth the visit. Great food, warm service, and a lovely atmosphere. I truly loved the experience and would definitely recommend this place.

featured_reviews.name: Priyanka Jadhav
featured_reviews.review_text: The Big Fish and co is located near Sena Bhavan, Dadar. The food was good. Do try the Tisrya Masala — it was good. The bhakri was very soft, and the chicken ghee roast was also nice. Overall, a great place for seafood lovers

customer_updates.text:
The restaurant serves authentic Maharashtrian cuisine, and it was an outstanding experience. We started with Agri Matka and Chulivarcha Chicken, both of which were bursting with flavor. The Agri Matka had that traditional rustic touch, slow-cooked to perfection, while the Chulivarcha Chicken, prepared on a traditional clay stove, was smoky, tender, and incredibly delicious.

For starters, we tried the Prawn Sukka, which was a perfect blend of spices, with succulent prawns cooked in a dry, aromatic masala. It was the ideal start to the meal. We also couldn't resist the Prawn Biryani, which was fragrant and loaded with juicy prawns. The balance of spices and flavors in every dish was just spot on.
Overall, this restaurant is a must-visit for anyone craving authentic Maharashtrian food. Every dish was prepared with care, and the flavors stayed true to the region's culinary heritage. I can't wait to go back and try more!

featured_reviews.name: H Nanda
featured_reviews.review_text:
Located in Dadar, on the busy gokhale road, this non veg restaurant is known for sea food.  Restaurant is clean and well maintained.   Service is also clean and neat.  While sea food is good, chicken items are quite ordinary ( tried chicken biryani, butter chicken - nothing great).  On the other hand prawn dishes were good.  Food preparation is Maharashtrian flavor.   Prices are reasonable.
Peak times and peak days would have some wait time to get the table.  Parking is a major problem,  though they have valet service board, I do know where are going to park your vehicle.   Nearest known parking is near Shivaji Park or Kohinoor mall ( BMC  Parking), both about a kilometer away.  I have had food here about five to six times.  Worth a try.

The decor was quite nice and warm. As we seated down the waiter was quick to attend us.

We visited for lunch and thus ordered a Surmai Thali. They also had option of Pomfret and Bombil. Apart from that we ordered Prawns tawa fry. We were enquiring if we should order a glass of Kokkum soul carry which were were advised against as they offered to serve us as much as we want with the food. We loved this gracious offer

The food did take about 15 mins to arrive but it was super good. We loved every bit of it. The music was very light thus allow us to have a conversation too.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Coast & Bloom at Dadar and it turned out to be a truly memorable dining experience that beautifully celebrates coastal and regional Indian flavors with a refined touch.

We began with the Lobster Thermidor, which was served in a rich, creamy mushroom sauce accompanied by sautéed vegetables, bread, and a perfectly cooked egg. The dish was indulgent, flavorful, and luxuriously satisfying. Alongside, we had the Tandoori Prawns, which carried an excellent smoky char from the tandoor. Paired with fresh green chutney and a sweet-tangy mango pickle, the combination elevated the entire starter experience.

For the main course, we opted for the Malvani Fish Curry with Ravas. The fish was exceptionally fresh, tender, and cooked to perfection, soaking beautifully in the aromatic Malvani gravy. We also tried the Chettinad Chicken, which had a bold, spicy profile and was packed with deep, authentic flavors.

To complement the curries, we had Malabar Parotta, Ghavane, and Chilli Cheese Garlic Naan. Each bread brought a different texture and paired wonderfully with the gravies, with the ghavane being a particularly delightful and unique accompaniment.

We also enjoyed Solkadi, which perfectly balanced the meal with its refreshing, lightly spiced tanginess. For drinks, we tried the Ratamba (kokum-based), Navy Punch, and Ginger Ale, all of which were refreshing and well-crafted.

To end the meal, we had the Crab Meat Fried Rice. While pleasant, this was comparatively simpler in flavor and had lesser crab meat than expected.

What truly stood out, beyond the food, was the exceptional service. The staff member assisting us went above and beyond — offering curry samples when we were confused between options and even showing us the raw fish to help us understand the portion and quality we would be served. Such thoughtful hospitality added immense value to the experience.

The entire meal came to ₹8,236, and considering the quality of ingredients, variety of dishes, and outstanding service, it felt well worth the price.

Coast & Bloom is a must-visit for anyone who appreciates coastal cuisine served with elegance, authenticity, and warm hospitality.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited Malhar recently for lunch and ordered a variety of dishes, including Crab Lollipop, Prawns Koliwada, White Rice, Rava Bombil, and Agri-style Chicken Curry. We had also planned to try Amboli and Bhakri, but unfortunately, both were out of stock.

The Crab Lollipop and Prawns Koliwada were flavorful and well-prepared. However, the Agri-style Chicken Curry did not meet expectations. The use of garam masala was overpowering, and the excessive black pepper (kalimiri) affected the overall taste, though the dish was still edible.

The ambience of the restaurant was very beautiful, but I noticed some issues with cleanliness. For example, one of the glasses provided still had food particles stuck on the edge where a person drinks. I requested the steward to replace the glass; he took the dirty one but forgot to bring a new glass altogether, leaving me to drink directly from the bottle.

While the food was average overall, I was particularly disappointed with the service. Both the steward and the captain seemed uninterested and inattentive. Despite repeated requests, it took them over 15 minutes to bring tissues, even when asked clearly and politely.

Additionally, the Prawns Koliwada was served nearly 40 minutes later, after we had almost finished our main course. At that time, only 3–4 tables were occupied in the restaurant, so such a delay was unjustified. When I raised this issue with the captain, his casual response was, "Humare yaha thoda late hi hota hai." This type of attitude is not expected from a reputed establishment like Malhar.

In summary, although the ambience was nice and some dishes were good, the poor service, lack of attention to cleanliness, and indifferent staff attitude significantly impacted our overall dining experience.

featured_reviews.name: Chef Vaidehi Pathare
featured_reviews.review_text:
I had heard a lot about Gomantak in Dadar. On my recent visit, I finally decided to try it. It was raining heavily that day. Even then, the restaurant was completely packed. They have both AC and non-AC sections. I had to wait for about 15 to 20 minutes before getting a table. The crowd itself gave me a sense of how popular this place is among seafood lovers.

I ordered the Chicken Masala Thali and Crab Masala with Rice Bhakri. The Chicken Masala Thali came with Chicken Gravy, Chicken Rassa, Rice, Bhakri, Sol Kadi, and Salad. The Chicken Gravy had a rich flavour that reminded me of coastal Goan cooking. It had depth, warmth, and a balance of spice. The Chicken Rassa was light and paired beautifully with rice. The Sol Kadi worked as a refreshing sip after the gravies.

The Crab Masala was the highlight of the meal. The crab meat was fresh and sweet. The masala was layered with flavour and had the right amount of spice. The meat absorbed the masala so well that every bite felt satisfying. The staff even help you break the crab if needed, which makes it easier to enjoy. The Rice Bhakri was soft and thick. It soaked up the masala and gravies perfectly.

To finish, I ordered the Caramel Custard. It was smooth, light, and mildly sweet. It balanced the spice of the seafood dishes.

Gomantak is a family-style restaurant that focuses on good food rather than frills. The service was courteous and attentive. The prices are fair for the portions and quality. It is a reliable place in Dadar if you are looking for seafood that feels authentic and comforting.

Ratings:
Quality – 4/5
Quantity – 4.1/5
Service – 4/5
Price – ₹800 for 2 people

For more food experiences, follow @chefvaidehipathare on Instagram!

featured_reviews.name: shripad marathe
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you're craving authentic coastal flavors in Mumbai, Jai Hind Lunch Home in Dadar West is an absolute must-visit! Having heard great things about their multiple branches across Mumbai and Thane, I finally made it to their Dadar outlet, and what an experience it was!

The Food - Simply Outstanding!
Let me walk you through the feast we had:

The Special Agri Prawns were the star of the evening - perfectly marinated, succulent, and bursting with coastal spices. Each prawn was cooked to perfection, maintaining that delicate sweetness while packing a flavorful punch.

The Bombil Sandwich was a delightful surprise! Crispy on the outside, soft within, this Bombay Duck preparation showcased why this humble fish is so beloved in Mumbai cuisine.

Chicken Alishan Kebab - tender, juicy, and beautifully spiced. The char on these kebabs added a wonderful smoky dimension that had us reaching for more.

The Mutton Sukka deserves special mention - dry, spicy, and incredibly aromatic. The meat was fork-tender, and the masala coating was absolutely addictive. Perfect with some Vade, Neer Dosa or even on its own!

Surmai Thali was a complete meal in itself. The kingfish was fresh and expertly prepared, accompanied by perfectly portioned sides that complemented the main dish beautifully.

For desserts, the Kulfi was rich and creamy with authentic flavors, while the Caramel Custard was silky smooth with just the right amount of sweetness - a perfect ending to our seafood extravaganza.

The Ambiance & Entertainment

The restaurant has a warm, welcoming vibe that's perfect for both family dinners and catching up with friends. A special shoutout for their Thursday live music - it adds such a wonderful atmosphere to the dining experience! There's something magical about enjoying delicious coastal cuisine with live music in the background.

Great Value for Money

They have an interesting social media offer - tag them on Instagram or Facebook and get up to 10% off on bills over ₹1000 (valid Monday-Thursday all day, and Wednesday-Friday till 4 PM, for alcoholic beverages only). It's a clever way to engage with customers while offering genuine value!

Final Verdict

Jai Hind Lunch Home delivers on all fronts - authentic flavors, generous portions, reasonable prices, and a great atmosphere. Whether you're a seafood lover or enjoy good coastal/Mangalorean cuisine, this place won't disappoint. The fact that they've expanded to multiple locations speaks volumes about their consistency and quality.

Will definitely be returning to try more from their extensive menu. Highly recommended! 🦐🐟

The stuffed bombil is nice as a novelty dish to taste once but was outshone by surmai and chilli chicken. For mains we ordered prawns pulimunchi and sukka chicken with vade and Malabar paratha. Loved the vada and chicken combo! For desserts we ordered caramel custard and gulab jamun. Both were tasty and melt in the mouth kinds.

featured_reviews.name: Alok Shettigar
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re a seafood lover looking for authentic Mangalorean-style delicacies in Mumbai, Sion Lunch Home is the place to be. Located just a five-minute walk from Sion railway station, this eatery has been my go-to spot for the past two years, and I can confidently say it never disappoints.

Ambience & Seating

The place is clean and well-maintained, but it doesn’t have a very large seating capacity. Whether you opt for the AC or non-AC section, expect a waiting time—sometimes as long as 40 minutes to an hour. Due to its immense popularity, the restaurant does not accept reservations, so it’s always bustling with seafood enthusiasts.

Food & Specialties

The main reason for the crowd? The exceptional seafood, prepared in true Mangalorean style. I highly recommend trying their fish thalis and fish fries, which are consistently fresh and flavorful.

Must-Try Dishes:

Prawns Fry – Crispy, well-spiced, and utterly delicious.

Squid Fry – Perfectly cooked and packed with coastal flavors.

Bombil Fry – A Mumbai favorite that’s crispy on the outside, soft inside.

Pomfret Thali – A full-fledged meal featuring succulent pomfret fish.

Surmai Thali – A classic favorite for those who love kingfish.

Neer Dosa – Light, fluffy and an excellent companion to their flavorful gravies.

Mutton Sukka – My personal favorite; the spice blend is simply spot-on.

Fish Platters: A Family Favorite

If you’re visiting with family, the fish platters are a must-try. They offer a great variety and are perfect for sharing, ensuring you get to taste a bit of everything.

Final Verdict

Despite the long waiting time, the experience at Sion Lunch Home is always worth it. The food quality, authentic preparation, and reasonable prices make it one of the best places in Mumbai for seafood lovers. If you enjoy coastal cuisine, this spot should be at the top of your list!

featured_reviews.name: durgesh gawde
featured_reviews.review_text:
Jai Hind is a gem for seafood lovers, offering an impressive variety of dishes, generous portions, and prices that feel genuinely value-for-money. If you’re someone who appreciates fresh, well-cooked fish without burning a hole in your pocket, this restaurant easily stands out as one of the best options in the city.

One of the first things you notice at Jai Hind is the sheer range on the menu. From classics like Surmai Fry, Bombil Fry, Rawas Curry, and Prawns Koliwada to specials like Crab Masala and Tawa Pomfret, the restaurant ensures there’s something for every seafood enthusiast. What makes the experience even better is that the quality is consistent. The fish is fresh, perfectly marinated, and cooked with authentic coastal flavours that highlight Mumbai’s rich culinary heritage.

Quantity is another major plus. Unlike many seafood places where portions feel small for the price, Jai Hind gives you hearty servings that truly justify every rupee. Whether you order a thali or an à la carte dish, the plates come generously loaded, making it easy to share or enjoy as a filling meal on your own. Their fish thalis, in particular, are a standout—they offer a balanced combination of fried fish, curry, rice, chapati, and sides, making it both wholesome and satisfying.

The pricing is surprisingly reasonable, especially considering the rising cost of seafood in the city. For the quality and quantity provided, the restaurant manages to keep its rates fair, which is a big reason people return. It’s a great place for regular seafood cravings without feeling guilty about overspending.

The ambience is simple, clean, and comfortable—nothing overly fancy, but perfectly suited for a relaxed and enjoyable meal. Service is prompt, friendly, and attentive, with staff who are happy to recommend dishes based on your taste preferences.

A Seafood Disaster – Masooli Restaurant

Visited Masooli expecting good seafood. What we got was very disappointing.

We ordered crab garlic, surmai garlic masala, bombil thecha fry, surmai green masala, rice with plain fish curry, solkadi and lime soda. The only real savior in the entire meal was the surmai green masala. The solkadi and lime soda were fine.

Everything else was a letdown. The fish curry had no tanginess, no salt, no flavour. It tasted flat and unfinished. For a seafood restaurant, getting a basic fish curry wrong is shocking. The crab garlic and bombil thecha fry were also disappointing.

I even called the waiter and asked him to taste the fish curry himself. He did not argue or defend it. He was so sure I was right that he did not even attempt to try it.

Service was good and the waiter was polite and attentive. But good service cannot save bad food.

Prices are high, but the taste does not justify it at all. Very disappointing experience. Would not return.

🌴 A Heartwarming Goan Experience at a Portuguese Restaurant 🌴

Dining at this Goan Portuguese restaurant was truly a delightful experience. From the first bite to the last note of live music, everything felt authentic, soulful, and unforgettable.

The food was absolutely amazing—rich in flavor, perfectly balanced, and deeply rooted in Goan tradition. Every dish reflected care, passion, and mastery of recipes passed down through generations.

⭐ Special Dishes We Tried:

Coconut Cashew Bhaji – A standout vegetarian dish, creamy, mildly spiced, and incredibly comforting. The coconut and cashew combination was simply delicious.

Surmai Fish Kalvam – A must-try for fish lovers. Fresh surmai cooked in a flavorful Goan-style curry that was bold, aromatic, and unforgettable.

Live Music by Uncle – The soulful live music added magic to the evening, creating a warm and joyful Goan vibe that elevated the entire dining experience.

What truly made this place special was the personal touch. The owner personally visited every table, warmly sharing the inspiring journey of how the restaurant began. He spoke about his wife’s culinary journey and her exceptional talent as a cook—the heart behind the delicious recipes served here. Listening to their story made the food taste even better, knowing it comes from passion, dedication, and love.

The restaurant has grown into multiple branches, including international locations, and it’s easy to see why. This place is not just about food—it’s about culture, stories, and genuine hospitality.

✨ Highly recommended for anyone who loves authentic Goan cuisine, soulful music, and heartfelt hospitality. A place you’ll want to visit again and again.

Goa Portuguese is a must stop in my every visit to Mumbai (from USA). This place has such a fun vibe with awesome food. There Goan and malvani dishes remind me of my mom’s home cooking.   We always start with Bombay duck fry and shrimp koliwada. Then the order including tisarya sukhe, chicken xacuti, pomfret / surmai dishes, amboli, vade continues so much that we get warned by the waiter ‘jara jast hoil ho’ (might be little to much). But we love their food so much that the warning, even though correct, gets ignored.
Even after visiting so many times, we have managed to touch very less amounts of dishes offered. Must increase our visits.
This time was lucky to meet with Dr. Suhas Awchat (co-founder). A warm personality and all the praise for master chef, Mrs. Deepa Awchat (he openly gave the credit of starting and owning the restaurant completely  to her, indicating that after army, she is his boss 😀).
Awesome food, fun atmosphere, good - helpful staff. Definitely a must visit place.

featured_reviews.name: Surajit Roy
featured_reviews.review_text:
We were influenced by a Fat Foody influencer to try this restaurant. Frankly, we were quite disappointed!

We ordered a surmai thali with chapati, one pomfret thali with neer dosa. The waiter suggested we order a starter dish, as the main course would take some time.

We had a long wait in store for us! In fact, the chicken starter arrived just a few minutes before the thalis!

The chicken boneless starter was a batter-fried item with lots of curry leaves. Since the batter was a ground rice batter, the jacket was hard!

The fish thali had a thinner than normal surmai slice and a small pomfret. There was a beetroot bhaji, a small bowl of jawla fried, a curry and a glass of solkadi. Lots of curry leaves! When it comes to fish thalis, we refer to the quality and size available at Gomantak at Plaza, Dadar West. This one gets a 3/5 compared to Gomantak.

The wait time is quite long, considering the fact that it was just 15-20% full. They need to work on this.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Restaurant Review: Super Anna Spot, Sion

Just visited the newly opened Coconut lunch home,Super Anna Spot in Sion, and it’s a hidden gem for lovers of Mangalorean cuisine. The standout for me was the benne dosa—soft, rich, and buttery, with that perfect golden crisp that melts in your mouth. It had that authentic South Indian street-style flavor which immediately transported me to Karnataka.

I also tried the chicken green masala, which paired beautifully with both neer dosa and cheese garlic naan. The curry was flavorful, slightly spicy, and had just the right amount of heat to awaken your taste buds without overwhelming them. The kori roti chicken was another hit—a traditional delicacy that was well-executed with crunchy roti pieces soaking up the rich, spicy gravy.

What makes this place special is the wide variety of Mangalorean dishes they offer, which you rarely find in the city. The flavors are bold, authentic, and well-balanced. Portions are generous and pricing feels reasonable for the quality and uniqueness of the food.

Definitely worth a visit if you’re looking to explore something beyond the usual. Super Anna Spot brings a true coastal vibe to the heart of Sion. I’ll be going back for more!

The quantity in each thali was perfect for one adult. If at all I have to complain then I would say, I missed the small portion of Suka Jawla (dry baby shrimp) that is also served as part of the seafood thali in my town.

The service was prompt and the staff was welcoming. Hygiene is taken care of. The place is tiny and very modestly done up, so if you value the ambience as much as your food, then this isn't the place for you. Free Street Parking is available.

If you are craving for good authentic Malvani Food… Sadichha is just the place for you.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Having visited countless seafood restaurants across Goa, the Konkan region, and Mumbai, I can confidently say that Jai Hind tops my list.

Yes, there’s almost always a long waiting line, and at times you may be asked to share a table with other diners. But honestly, that’s only because the place is packed with people who keep coming back for the food. And once you taste it, you’ll understand why.

The seafood is fresh, flavorful, and cooked to perfection. What makes the experience even better is the value for money. Unlike many places that charge extra for every little thing, the thali here is genuinely generous and unlimited, you can ask for refills of the items in your thali as many times as you’d like.

Great food, excellent portions, and prices that feel justified. If you’re a seafood lover, the wait is absolutely worth it.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Dishes we had:
1. Crab Lollipop: 6/10
2. Thalis with Rice Bhakaris
-a. Surmai: 10/10
-b. Pomfret: 9/10
-c. Bombil: 7/10
3. Gulab Jamun: 3/10
4. Fresh Lime Soda: 8/10

Crab Lollipop wasn't great. I have had better elsewhere.
It lacked the basic crab taste and the coating too was very mild on flavor.

The thalis were awesome. The fish were very fresh and tasty that it made our day. Surmai was the best. It had the best flavor, followed by Pomfret and then the Bombil. Surmai and Pomfret were rawa fry with little masala. It was just plain batter fry for the Bombil. We make better Bombil fry at home, so yeah.
The rice bhakari tasted awesome when it was hot.
Dry Prawns/Jhinga/Javla tasted good with the bhakari.
The pomfret fish and curry was very fresh and tasty.
Solkadhi was chilled, felt refreshing and tasted good.

Gulab Jamun was the worst. Hard, dry and low on flavor.

Restaurant is smaller compared to the one near kemps corner. Cleanliness was decent. No washrooms. Only a basin is available. No Queue when we arrived at 8pm. But a queue started building later on.

Group of 4. Saturday Dinner. Mid April 2026.

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ 5/5 – Authentic Malvani Taste at Its Best!

Visited Malvani Klub Restaurant at Lalbaugh with my wife, and we were genuinely impressed with the food, service, and overall experience. We ordered the Bangda Thali and Prawns Thali, and both were absolutely delicious. The Prawns Fry served as a starter was perfectly spiced and crispy, while the Solkadi was refreshing and authentic.

The Bangda fry in the thali had that perfect Malvani masala flavour, and the curries were rich, aromatic, and truly reminded us of homely Maharashtrian coastal food. The prawns curry was equally flavourful, and the chapatis were soft and fresh.

Apart from the excellent food, the staff deserves a special mention — very polite, friendly, and attentive. They made the dining experience even better with their warm hospitality.

If you love Maharashtrian or Malvani cuisine, this place is a must-visit. Highly recommended!

featured_reviews.name: Nitant Pandhare
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Coastal Paradise for Seafood Lovers! 🦀✨
Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

If you are looking for authentic Malvani flavors in Mumbai, Malvani Klub is an absolute gem. We visited recently and were blown away by the freshness of the seafood and the richness of their traditional masalas.

The Highlights:

Starters: We started with the Fried Bombil and Prawns Fry. The Bombil (Bombay Duck) was perfectly crisp on the outside and buttery-soft inside—just the way it should be! The prawns were succulent, fresh, and seasoned to perfection.

The Thali Experience:

Surmai Thali: The fish was a generous size, well-marinated, and paired beautifully with the authentic Malvani rassa.

Chicken Komdi Vade Thali: The vade were fluffy and hot, making them the perfect companion to the spicy, flavorful chicken curry.

Crab Thali: A true standout! The crab was meaty and the gravy had that deep, soulful coastal spice kick.

Kolambi Bhaat: This was a revelation! Fragrant rice cooked with juicy prawns and a blend of aromatic spices. It’s a must-order if you want a hearty, one-pot Malvani meal.

Solkadhi: No Malvani meal is complete without this. Their Solkadhi was refreshing, creamy, and had the perfect balance of kokum and garlic to cleanse the palate.

The food here is amazingly awesome and truly authentic. The portions are satisfying, and the taste reminds you of a home-cooked meal in the Konkan belt. Whether you're a hardcore seafood fan or a chicken lover, this place will not disappoint!

Recommendation: Go hungry, and definitely don't miss the Kolambi Bhaat!
